summary:
Gombe State operates two overlapping criminal regimes against same-sex conduct. The Sharia Penal Code Law 2001, signed on 23 November 2001, is Gombe's own enacted statute; Human Rights Watch's 2004 report lists Gombe among the twelve northern states that had adopted Sharia into criminal legislation by 2002, with Sharia courts holding criminal jurisdiction over Muslims beyond federal law.

The penalties under Gombe's statute are severe and gendered. Gombe, Jigawa, Kano and Zamfara share a sodomy offence punishing unmarried men with 100 lashes plus one year's imprisonment and married men with stoning to death (rajm); the lesbianism offence carries up to 50 lashes plus imprisonment of up to six months. Gombe defines gross indecency in its own formulation as 'any sexual offence against the normal or usual standards of behaviour.' The enacted statutory text criminalises same-sex conduct by men and women beyond the federal code.

The UK Home Office country-of-origin information note (June 2025) on sexual orientation and gender identity in Nigeria records that Islamic law applies to Muslims in the twelve northern states, including Gombe, and criminalises same-sex sexual acts both between men and between women; the maximum penalty for 'sodomy' for men is death in all twelve states, and penalties for 'lesbianism' range from death to flogging and imprisonment. The note includes a dedicated section on enforcement of Sharia provisions and the attitude of the hisbah (morality police).

Gombe has enforced these provisions in a mass arrest. In October 2023 the Gombe State Command of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps raided a gathering at Duwa Plaza along the Bauchi-Gombe Expressway that was preparing a same-sex wedding, arresting 76 people. State PRO Buhari Sa'ad told reporters that 59 males were detained, 21 of whom wilfully confessed to being homosexuals, with 17 females present, and that they would be charged in court for 'social vice; a crime in Gombe State.' The Guardian of 23 October 2023 independently confirmed the arrests, with Gombe NSCDC Commandant Mohammed Muazu confirming them and spokesperson Buhari Saad stating that 21 of the 59 detained males were involved in gay activities while the remaining males and 17 females were invited guests and onlookers; officers also voiced concern over the participants' ages.
tangentialFactors:
The October 2023 Gombe raid is one of several documented mass arrests at social venues across Nigeria in this period, alongside the arrest of more than 100 party-goers at a hotel in Asaba, Delta State, in June 2018, 57 young men at Egbeda, Lagos, in August 2018, and the 'Warri 67' in Warri, Delta State, in August 2023. Raw counts of such arrests track both population and enforcement intensity; the figures are reported as raw counts without per-capita denominators.

Gombe's Sharia framework sits within a wider northern pattern: the twelve northern states have all adopted Sharia into criminal legislation, and the UK Home Office records the death penalty as the maximum for male sodomy in all twelve. Gombe's own 2001 statute shares its sodomy and lesbianism provisions with Jigawa, Kano and Zamfara.
localsOnly:
Gombe's Sharia Penal Code Law 2001 applies its own penalties to residents: unmarried men face 100 lashes plus one year's imprisonment for sodomy, married men face stoning to death (rajm), and the lesbianism offence carries up to 50 lashes plus up to six months' imprisonment. Gombe's own definition of gross indecency covers 'any sexual offence against the normal or usual standards of behaviour.'

Sharia courts in Gombe hold criminal jurisdiction over Muslims beyond federal law, per Human Rights Watch's 2004 report. The hisbah (morality police) operate within this framework, as documented in the UK Home Office's June 2025 note.

The 76 people arrested in the October 2023 raid at Duwa Plaza were to be charged in Gombe State court; 21 of the 59 detained males had confessed. Officers raised concerns about the ages of participants, indicating possible underage exposure in the charging decisions.
outOfScopeNotes:
The outcome of the October 2023 Gombe mass arrests, including whether charges were filed and how the 76 detainees were ultimately adjudicated, is not sourced in the inventory and remains unresolved.

Whether the hisbah in Gombe specifically has conducted documented enforcement actions against gender-nonconforming or trans residents is not sourced here; the UK Home Office note addresses the hisbah generally across the twelve northern states.

Whether Gombe's Sharia Penal Code Law 2001 has been amended, challenged, or partially suspended since 2001 is not addressed in the available sources.
